extraction.name: Arabic-Nougat
extraction.description: A suite of OCR models for converting Arabic book pages into structured Markdown text, fine-tuned on a synthetic paired image-Markdown dataset.
extraction.creator: Mohamed A. Rashad
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The primary training dataset arabic-img2md was created by scraping HTML content from the Hindawi website, converting it to PDFs, and extracting Markdown text to form paired samples of Arabic book pages and Markdown representations.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: HTML content from the Hindawi website, converted into PDFs and paired with extracted Markdown text; additionally, over 8,500 books were used to extract 1.1 billion Arabic tokens for arabic-books.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Collected HTML was converted to PDFs and Markdown was extracted to create paired image-Markdown samples.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: HTML content was transformed into PDFs and then into paired Arabic book page images and Markdown representations for model training.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset labels are Markdown representations paired with Arabic book page images, generated automatically from scraped HTML content rather than manually annotated.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work aims to support digitization of underrepresented languages like Arabic and provide resources for future Arabic OCR and NLP research.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The arabic-img2md dataset is derived from Hindawi web content and may not generalize well to other Arabic domains such as scientific, religious, or historical documents.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include hallucination in arabic-small-nougat, repetition in larger models, dataset bias toward Hindawi content, scalability challenges for training large models, limited cross-script generalization testing, and difficulty with highly irregular or multi-modal layouts.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluation for Arabic OCR and Markdown extraction from Arabic book pages; recommended use includes arabic-base-nougat for general text extraction and arabic-large-nougat for lengthy or complex documents.

name.evidence: We introduce Arabic-Nougat , a suite of OCR models designed to convert Arabic book pages into structured Markdown text.

description.evidence: We introduce Arabic-Nougat , a suite of OCR models designed to convert Arabic book pages into structured Markdown text. Building on Meta’s Nougat architecture, Arabic-Nougat includes three specialized models: arabic-small-nougat ,arabic-base-nougat , and arabic-large-nougat . These models are fine-tuned using a synthetic dataset, arabic-img2md , consisting of 13.7k paired samples of Arabic book pages and their Markdown representations.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: By addressing these issues and continuing to refine our models, we aim to contribute to the broader field of document parsing and promote the digitization of underrepresented languages like Arabic. Additionally, the open-sourcing of arabic-books , a 1.1 billion-token dataset extracted from Arabic literature, provides a valuable resource for future research in Arabic NLP and OCR [14].

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Dataset Biases: Thearabic-img2md dataset, derived from Hindawi’s web content, may not generalize well to other domains of Arabic text, such as scientific, religious, or historical documents.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: While Arabic-Nougat marks a significant advancement in Arabic OCR, several limitations remain: •Hallucination in arabic-small-nougat ... •Repetition in larger models ... •Dataset Biases ... may not generalize well to other domains ... •Scalability Challenges ... •Cross-Script Generalization ... has not been extensively tested ... •Complex Layouts ... may require additional preprocessing or model adaptations

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: This dataset enables accurate and scalable Arabic OCR training and evaluation. For practical applications, we recommend using arabic-base-nougat for general text extraction tasks and arabic-large-nougat for lengthy or complex documents.
